items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: Then when we got to the train station, Thigpen wasn't there. But Dick Vance was there.

ctx.x: So we got ready to go to Chicago. I didn't want to leave New York. I ended up getting a little bit more money than he was willing to pay. I got five dollars more. I think everybody was supposed to get... I don't know, to tell you the truth. He said everybody else was getting fifty-five or sixty, or something like that, and he gave me seventy. So you know, he could tell me anything. But anyway, when he came up with that seventy dollars, I decided to go.

Then when we got to the train station, Thigpen wasn't there. But Dick Vance was there. And he looked kind of strange, because he was... We were all whistling, you know how they do in the band, me and Buster and the (?) people. We was just going... I got married that same day, too. I got married that day, and it was very lucky, going to Chicago... We told the conductor... You know, because we was in the coach. And he gave us one of those staterooms; they called them staterooms. He gave us one of those staterooms,…
When we got there, it was about 26 below. Whew! Man,
